summary: This note argues that national festivals are more than holidays: they carry a nation's history, beliefs and aspirations, and they shape and reflect societal norms. It surveys festivals around the world, from Jidai Matsuri and Rio Carnival to Deepavali and Canada Day, with commentary from scholars and organizers. The main themes are cultural transmission, collective belonging, adaptation of tradition, and multiculturalism.
one_line: An analysis of how national festivals worldwide transmit culture, build collective identity, adapt over time and promote multiculturalism, illustrated with dated examples and expert quotes.
key_facts: Jidai Matsuri, one of Japan's three great festivals known for historical re-enactments, was celebrated in Kyoto on October 7, 2023.
Professor Sato Haruki of the Tokyo University of Arts called Jidai Matsuri a 'living museum' that imparts values of honor, community, and continuity.
The Rio Carnival in Brazil was held on February 15, 2024, and conveys narratives of resistance and celebration of Afro-Brazilian culture, according to cultural anthropologist Luisa Fernanda.
Gion Matsuri in Kyoto is a month-long July festival with a history dating back to 869 CE; historian Yamamoto Takeshi called it 'a testament to the resilience and solidarity of the community.'
The Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City on November 24, 2023 features giant balloons and reenacts a narrative of gratitude and cooperation between the Pilgrims and Native Americans.
Ghana's Homowo Festival, celebrated by the Ga people on September 5, 2023, symbolizes victory over a historic famine; sociologist Ama Biney links it to sustainability and climate change themes.

St. Patrick's Day on March 17, 2024 was celebrated by millions worldwide; historian O'Connor Declan of the University of Dublin says it merges Irish mythology, Christianity, and the narrative of emigration.

Deepavali, celebrated October 24, 2023 across India and the diaspora, renews social fabric through sweets, lamps and firecrackers, which Dr. Aruna Sharma says reinforce familial links and community cohesion.
La Tomatina in Spain took place on August 31, 2023; Dr. Maria Vargas of the University of Valencia describes it as steeped in a post-war spirit of abundance and exuberance.
France's Bastille Day on July 14, 2023 featured fireworks and military parades reflecting liberty, equality, and fraternity.
Mariana Costa organized the Lisbon Festas de Santo Antonio on June 13, 2023, and says heritage must be balanced with contemporary expressions.
Nigeria's Festac festival, slated for December 1, 2023, is directed by playwright Chibuike Ibe, who says it reinterprets cultural milestones for a changing society.
Canada Day, celebrated July 1, 2024, showcases Canada's mosaic of cultures; sociologist Jean-Michel Fortier calls it 'policy turned practice.'
